title: Oncall cadence, game-day scripting, and customer signal protocol
author: Ana Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook defines Redwood’s operational cadence for oncall rotations, provides ready-to-run game-day scripts for common failure modes, and standardizes the customer signal protocol used for status page and targeted customer notifications. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, service owners, and incident commanders.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-detect and time-to-recover for production degradations.
- Provide reproducible, testable game-day scenarios that validate end-to-end tooling (alerts, status page, comm templates).
- Ensure consistent, clear customer communication tied to objective signals.

Scope:
- Production services for Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private control-plane components.
- Incident types covered: SLO breaches (latency/error-rate), capacity exhaustion (GPU pool saturated), model-serving regressions (inference errors/invalid outputs), control-plane outages (auth, billing), and region failovers.
- Out of scope: localized developer environment issues and feature branch CI failures.

Key Definitions:
- Incident Commander (IC): person coordinating response and cross-team communication.
- Oncall Engineer: first responder responsible for initial triage.
- Escalation Lead: second-tier SME to handle deeper remediation (e.g., runtime, infra).
- Customer Signal: a verifiable metric or event that warrants customer-facing comms (see section "Customer Signal Matrix").

Roles & Responsibilities:
1) Oncall Engineer (primary):
   - Acknowledge paging alerts within 5 minutes.
   - Run the appropriate runbook checklist for the alert type.
   - If containment not achieved in 15 minutes, request IC.

2) Incident Commander (IC):
   - Assemble responders and assign clear tasks.
   - Own the timeline and public comm cadence.
   - Decide on status page updates and severity classification.

3) Escalation Lead / SME:
   - Focus on remediation steps that require deep knowledge (kernel, GPUs, model graph).

4) Communications Lead (usually IC or delegated PM from customer-success):
   - Draft and publish status page entries and customer emails.

Oncall Cadence & Handoff:
- Rotation length: 7 days for primary oncall, 14 days for backup (shadow).
- Weekly handoff brief: automatic Slack post by rotation-bot containing open incidents, known issues, and any pending action items.
- Handoff checklist (must be completed in rotation-bot form):
  1. Confirm escalation contact list is current.
  2. Review SLO burn rate dashboard links.
  3. Confirm runbook ownership annotations.

Escalation Ladder (example):
- Pager alert -> Oncall Engineer (5 min ack) -> Escalation Lead (15 min) -> IC (30 min) -> Exec Notification (60+ min for Sev1).

Customer Signal Matrix (select signals that require public communication):
- Severity: Sev1 (complete outage or >90% API error rate), Sev2 (partial outage, large SLO breach), Sev3 (isolated customer impact).
- Objective signals: sustained 5m error rate > 10% for Hosted API, 5m median tail latency (p95) > 2x baseline, Dedicated: active queued requests > 80% of pool for 10+ min, Control-plane auth failures > 1% of requests for 5+ min.
- When any objective signal is met, trigger status page entry and classify customers by impact for targeted messages.

Runbook Templates (use as copy/paste checklists):
- SLO breach (high error-rate or high latency):
  1. Validate alerts and check raw traces dashboard: /dashboards/slo-burn-rate.
  2. Identify rollback candidate model versions or scalar config changes in nightly config PRs.
  3. Check recent deploys: `git log --since=2h --services=service-name`.
  4. If model-serving: verify KV cache health and GPU memory pressure via `nvidia-smi` and `runtime-inspect --node`.
  5. Mitigation options: scale replicas, enable degraded-mode routing to small-quantized model variant, or route to Dedicated fallback region.
  6. If containment not achieved in 15 minutes, IC publishes initial status page as "Investigating".

- GPU pool saturation (Dedicated):
  1. Confirm queue length and active allocation: /dashboards/gpu-pool-util.
  2. Identify noisy tenants via token-level cost telemetry.
  3. Apply emergency throttling policy for offending route: `redwood admin rate-limit set --route <route> --qps 10 --reason "noisy-tenant"`.
  4. Provision burst capacity if reserve pool available.
  5. Notify sales/CS for impacted customers and map to SLA entitlements.

- Control-plane auth failures:
  1. Check KMS/HSM and OIDC provider health.
  2. Validate certificate rotations: `openssl s_client -connect auth.redwood.internal:443 -showcerts`.
  3. If certificates rotated incorrectly, fallback to previous cert bundle and roll forward with correct chain.

Status Page & Customer Communications (templates below):
- Status page template (short form):
  Title: [Investigating] Reduced inference throughput for Hosted API in us-west-2
  Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or timeouts.
  Latest update: We are investigating increased queue times in the inference tier. Oncall engineers are actively diagnosing and have isolated a throttling condition.
  Next update: 30 minutes or when we have a remediation plan.
  Owner: Incident Commander: @<IC-slack-handle>

- Customer targeted email (template):
  Subject: Immediate notice: Intermittent inference latency in us-west-2
  Body: Hello <Customer> team,

  We want to let you know we are currently investigating intermittent inference latency affecting a subset of requests routed to us-west-2. Our oncall team has identified increased queueing in the inference pool and is validating a mitigation plan (scaling + temporary routing to quantized variants). We estimate a remediation window of 30–60 minutes.

  Impact: Potentially higher latency or request timeouts for models served in the region.
  Mitigation: We are applying emergency throttling and routing changes to reduce queueing. No customer data is affected.

  We will follow up with updates on the status page: <status-link>. If you have specific SLAs impacted, reply to this message and we will prioritize direct assistance.

  — Redwood Support

Escalation Communication Checklist (IC must verify):
- Have we classified severity? (Sev1/Sev2/Sev3)
- Has a status page entry been created within 15 minutes of classification?
- Were customer-facing teams (sales, account execs) notified within 30 minutes for affected customers?

Game-Day Scripts (executable scenarios to validate process):
1) Scenario: Synthetic SLO degradation (Hosted API p95 spike)
   Script steps:
   - Inject synthetic load into staging mirrors with p95 latency doubled.
   - Verify that SLO burn rate alert fires in PagerDuty.
   - Execute oncall triage checklist and create a status page draft.
   - Validate that rotation-bot posts handoff notes and that comm templates can be sent from the status tool.
   Success criteria: Alerts, paging, status updates, and CS notifications are successful end-to-end.

2) Scenario: GPU pool noisy-tenant isolation (Dedicated)
   Script steps:
   - Simulate burst of queued allocations from test-tenant.
   - Confirm throttling policy triggers and noisy-tenant identification matches telemetry.
   - Apply emergency rate-limit and observe queue length return to baseline.
   Success criteria: Noisy tenant correctly throttled, metrics return to normal within 20 minutes, and dedicated alert suppressed post-mitigation.

Game Day Playbook (run cadence):
- Quarterly full-scale game day (all hands SRE + platform + CS).
- Monthly focused mini-drills (1 hour) for specific runbooks (auth, GPU, model-serving).
- After each game day: publish an exercise report with findings, owners, and remediation tickets.

Postmortem & RCA Template (mandatory for Sev1/Sev2 with >30 min customer impact):
- Title: [Postmortem] Short description + service affected
- Summary: 3–4 sentence customer-facing summary.
- Impact: list of affected customers, regions, SLOs missed, duration.
- Timeline: chronological bullet list with timestamps (UTC) of detection, actions, and recovery.
- Root cause: concise technical cause.
- Contributing factors: systemic or process gaps.
- Corrective actions: short-term and long-term (owner + due date).
- Validation plan: how we will verify the fix (dashboards, unit tests, game-days).
- Learning: changes to runbooks or oncall cadence.

Monitoring & Dashboards (minimum set for each service):
- SLO burn rate dashboard (5m, 1h windows).
- Request-latency histogram (p50/p95/p99).
- Error rate by route and token bucket.
- Queue depth and GPU memory pressure.
- External dependencies (OIDC, KMS) success rates.

Alert Threshold Examples (reference):
| Metric | Threshold | Pager | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API error rate (5m) | > 5% | P1 | Sev2->Sev1 if > 10% |
| p95 latency (5m) | > 2x baseline | P1 | Use regional baselines |
| GPU queue length | > 80% capacity (10m) | P1 | Dedicated pools only |
| Auth failures | > 1% | P2 | Control-plane impact |

Testing & Runbook Ownership:
- Every runbook must have a documented owner and a test that runs at least annually.
- Owners update runbook after any incident; review cadence is quarterly.

Automation & Tooling Integration:
- rotation-bot manages schedule and posts weekly handoff notes.
- incident-bot templates status page drafts and pushes to /statuspage-api.
- escalation-bot performs automatic paging escalation at configurable intervals.

Oncall Wellness & Burn Mitigation:
- Max consecutive paid rotations: 6 months; re-evaluate heavy rotations with manager.
- Silent paging hours: 22:00–06:00 local (only P0 pages unless explicitly opted in).
- Psychological safety: All responders are expected to avoid blame in public write-ups; focus on remediations and learning.

Appendix A — Example CLI commands and snippets:
- Check recent deploys: `git --no-pager log --since="2 hours ago" --pretty=format:"%h %s (%an)" -- services/service-a`
- Query GPU pool: `redwood infra pool describe --name gpu-pool-usw2 --json`
- Apply emergency throttling: `redwood admin rate-limit set --route conversions --qps 5 --reason "noisy-tenant"`

Appendix B — Post-game checklist:
1. Write exercise report and tag owners.
2. Create remediation JIRA with clear acceptance criteria.
3. Schedule runbook updates in the next weekly ops review.
